tools.name: get_latest_fundamentals
tools.description: The most recent reported value of each metric for one ticker, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Use it for a company's current figures, or with as_of for what had been filed by a given day; call search_companies first if you have a name rather than a ticker. Inputs: ticker (e.g. AAPL, 2330.TW, 005930.KS, 0403091220.BE, 775670417.FR, CC21860.NZC, and 10238429.EE, 5560356163.SE, 47239255.SK, 40003032949.LV where get_coverage lists them, and 96002925948.AU for Australia's tax figures); metric (comma-separated; a name we do not hold is left out); as_of (only filings dated on or before that day). On a free key, a company outside the full-history sample answers from its most recent reported fiscal year only (history_depth says so) and as_of needs a licence or an evaluation key. Each metric is its own latest value, so two metrics can come from different periods; a quarterly fp is ONE quarter's figure, not a year; check `stale` (true: the company has filed since without this metric, so the figure is not current). Before using the figures: they are as filed, each keyed to its filing date (`filed`) as its market records it (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). .TW quarterly values are already SINGLE-QUARTER amounts: do not difference adjacent quarters. For a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR quarter containing the period end, not the company's fiscal quarter. Each reply's `market_notes` and `schema` give the per-market caveats (solo or group accounts, lawful gaps, charities, flags in `form`); read them before interpreting a figure. Detailed line items follow local accounting rules and keep the filed sign (capex is negative in Taiwan and Japan): call get_data_dictionary before comparing them across markets. When you relay figures, keep the reply's `attribution` and `licence` notices with them.

metric.description: Comma-separated metrics, e.g. revenue,net_income. Omit for all.

as_of.description: Filing-date cut-off, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2022-01-01). Defaults to today.

tools.name: get_fundamentals_history
tools.description: The stored figures for one ticker, one row per metric and period, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Use it for trends and for what was on file at a past date. Inputs: ticker, metric (comma-separated), from (earliest period end), as_of (only filings dated on or before that day). On a free key, a company outside the full-history sample answers with its most recent reported fiscal year only: full_history false and history_depth say so, and older filings exist. Long histories are capped at 250 rows, keeping the most recent rows of EVERY metric (per_metric says how many of each); narrow with metric/from for the rest. Before using the figures: they are as filed, each keyed to its filing date (`filed`) as its market records it (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). .TW quarterly values are already SINGLE-QUARTER amounts: do not difference adjacent quarters. For a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR quarter containing the period end, not the company's fiscal quarter. Each reply's `market_notes` and `schema` give the per-market caveats (solo or group accounts, lawful gaps, charities, flags in `form`); read them before interpreting a figure. Detailed line items follow local accounting rules and keep the filed sign (capex is negative in Taiwan and Japan): call get_data_dictionary before comparing them across markets. When you relay figures, keep the reply's `attribution` and `licence` notices with them.

as_of.description: Filing-date cut-off, YYYY-MM-DD: only filings dated on or before that day

from.description: Earliest period end to include, YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Look up the ticker for a company name or partial symbol — 'Apple', 'TSMC', '2330', 'samsung', 'LVMH'. Use this first when the user names a company rather than a ticker, and check the market of the hit: a local subsidiary or a namesake in another country can share the name. Pass market (US, JP, TW, KR, FR, BE, DK, NZC) to search one market only. Results with market NZC are New Zealand registered charities, not listed companies.

market.description: Only this market: US, JP, TW, KR, FR, BE, DK or NZC

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Markets covered, ticker counts, history depth per market, the free-tier ticker list, the metric vocabulary, the source attributions that must travel with the data, and the licence the data is supplied under (with an evaluation key, its terms and end date).

tools.name: get_data_dictionary
tools.description: The data dictionary of the detailed line items: for every metric, its definition, which filed line each market reads it from (or why a market has none), and the measured share of that market's company-periods that carry it; the figures we calculate from them, with their formulas; and the rules that apply to all of them (dating, signs, annual-only cash-flow lines, small employers). Use it before comparing a line item across markets, or to learn what a line-item code means. Codes: trade_receivables, trade_and_other_receivables, inventories, trade_payables, trade_and_other_payables, ppe, noncurrent_assets, current_assets, current_liabilities, retained_earnings, depreciation_amortization, interest_expense, cash_flow_operating, capex, minority_interest, temporary_equity, land_and_buildings, land, buildings, pension_provisions, cost_of_materials, purchases_of_goods, purchases_of_materials, wages_and_salaries, operating_taxes, income_tax; calculated: free_cash_flow, working_capital, current_ratio, ebitda.
